name: People's Republic of China
native: 中华人民共和国 (Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó)

predecessors.name: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)
predecessors.text: the communist-held land at the proclamation: north and northeast China, Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, the lower Yangtze to Nanjing

predecessors.name: Republic of China
predecessors.text: the mainland south and west of the communist-held land of 1 October 1949: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Xinjiang, Qinghai and the rest

ledger.x: 1 October 1949: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China, capital at Beiping (Beijing).
ledger.cpn: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)

ledger.x: October 1949: Guangzhou passes to the Communists.
10 December 1949: Chengdu falls and resistance collapses.
December 1949: the rest of the mainland is Communist.
April 1950: Hainan falls to the People's Liberation Army.
7 October 1950: the PLA enters eastern Tibet and takes Chamdo.
23 May 1951: Chamdo's occupation ends in annexation under the Seventeen Point Agreement.
23 May 1951: Tibet is annexed by the Seventeen Point Agreement.
1957: China completes a road through Aksai Chin.
20 October 1962: China attacks along the Indian frontier.
21 November 1962: China declares a ceasefire and withdraws.

wars.name: Chinese Civil War
wars.outcome: Communist victory on the mainland: the Nationalist government left for Taiwan on 7 December 1949, resistance collapsed after Chengdu fell on 10 December 1949 and Hainan fell in April 1950.

wars.name: Annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China
wars.outcome: Chinese victory: Chamdo taken in October 1950; the Seventeen Point Agreement of 23 May 1951, accepted by the Dalai Lama in October 1951, brought U-Tsang and the Chamdo Region under Chinese control.

wars.name: Sino-Indian War
wars.outcome: Chinese victory with 'status quo ante bellum': China kept de facto control of Aksai Chin and withdrew from the North-East Frontier Agency to 20 km behind the line of actual control (1 December 1962).

certainty.note: The frontier with India (Aksai Chin, the North-East Frontier Agency) and with the Soviet Union and Burma was unsettled; the page does not date any boundary treaty.

23 border disputes since 1949, six of them unsettled (China page, closely paraphrased): most land frontiers are treaty lines, but the line of actual control with India stays soft and Hong Kong and Macau are sharp at their 1997 and 1999…
